# odyssey-088 (Odyssey 18.1–107) — Review

## Pass 1

Reviewer, pass 1 of 2. Method: runbook section 2 order — (1) every grammatical label, word-position claim and cross-reference in every note against the form and line; (2) Greek to `l` word by word; (3) `l` and `i` against each other; (4) remembered English in `i`; (5) quotation marks and `mark`; (6) new-renderings rows against the house table, and every repeated line or half-line against published English (all published parts odyssey-001 to 087 searched by script for any five-word run shared with a unit, then each hit read). `t` was never touched: the units' `t` strings are byte-identical before and after, and still join to the packet's 107 lines. No modern translation was opened or recalled; the house table (the whole of conventions.md, including rows appended after the Scansion section), the published parts and LSJ/Smyth-level knowledge were the only aids.

Checks that passed with no change: `ln` of every unit; `p` on the first unit of each of Murray's 16 paragraphs after line 1 (1, 10, 14, 32, 36, 40, 43, 50, 52, 58, 61, 66, 73, 75, 79, 88, 105); `v`; one `\n` in `l` per `\n` in `t`; no `\n` in `i`; typographic ’ and ‘ ’ only; no ASCII quotes in any field. Speech boundaries: ten speeches (10–13, 15–24, 26–31, 36–39, 43–49, 52–57, 61–65, 73–74, 79–87, 105–107), each with “ on its first unit and ” on its last in both `l` and `i`, and a `mark` on the first unit of each and on no other. The last unit of odyssey-087 (17.606, ἤδη γὰρ καὶ ἐπήλυθε δείελον ἦμαρ) is narration with no open quotation; the last unit here closes its speech, and the source shows narrator at 18.108 (ἦ ῥα καὶ ἀμφ’ ὤμοισιν…), so nothing runs into part 089.

Scansion flags: none in the packet, so no line was scanned by hand and no metrical sentence was added to any note.

`gloss.json` does not exist yet; its parses are for pass 2.

### Findings considered and refused

1. **ὁράασθαι (3), `l`/`i` ‘to look at’ against the note’s ‘to be looked at’.** The infinitive of respect after μέγας is passive in form and ‘great to look at’ is the English for it; the note describes the form, the translation gives the sense. Left.
2. **ἐρίζετον … μαχέσσασθαι (38), `i` ‘challenging each other to a fist fight’ against `l` ‘contending … to fight’.** ἐρίζω with an infinitive is ‘vie, strive’, and Antinous is describing two men squaring up; ‘challenging’ is within that range and reads as English. Left.
3. **κακοείμονας (40), `i` ‘the two ragged beggars’.** ‘two’ is not in the Greek but the note says the two beggars are meant and the context fixes it; ‘ragged’ is the ordinary English for ‘ill-clad’ and the word is in no house row. Left.
4. **ὑπερφιάλως (71), ‘beyond measure’ against the house ‘overweening’ for ὑπερφίαλος.** Not a conflict: the table row for 17.481 fixes exactly ‘beyond measure’ for the adverb, and odyssey-086.481 ships it. (The earlier shipped ‘overweeningly’ at odyssey-020.663 predates that row and is not this reviewer’s to change.) The note’s remark that this is not the adjective’s ‘overweening’ is true. Left.
5. **ἀνελόντα (16), `i` ‘even if he takes up a great deal to give’.** The reading is uncertain; the note says so in as many words and `i` follows the note’s reading. Left.
6. **ἥ μιν ἱκάνει (81), `i` ‘has come upon him’ against present ἱκάνει.** The present of a state that began earlier; English perfect is the natural rendering and `l` keeps the present. Left.
7. **ἐπιγνώωσι (30–31), `i` ‘see’ against `l` ‘take note of’.** Within the range of ἐπιγιγνώσκω in a purpose clause; the note gives both. Left.
8. **ἕλκε (101), note ‘imperfect, was dragging’ against `l`/`i` ‘dragged’.** Narrative imperfect; the note describes the form, not a different action. Left.
9. **‘The name echoes Ἶρις’ (6).** A remark about the name, not a claim about the rest of the poem; the note says the poem itself says only that he ran errands. Left.
10. **Interpretive remarks in the notes at 12 (Irus ‘the reluctant party’) and 22 (‘a beaten Irus will no longer trouble him’).** Both are marked as readings and neither contradicts `l` or `i`. Left.
11. **‘stuffed and roasted like a sausage’ (44).** An illustration, not a grammatical claim. Left.
12. **ἐπιλλίζουσιν ‘wink at’, `i` ‘winking’ (11).** The note’s ‘nods of encouragement’ is explanation, and `l`/`i` agree. Left.
13. **βαλὼν ἐν νηί (83), `i` reorders to ‘throw you into a black ship and send you’.** Same two acts; the order in English follows the sequence of events, and `l` keeps the Greek order. Left.
14. **Repeated lines.** 18.14, 18.72, 18.82, 18.93 and 18.104 agree word for word with the published English in both layers; 18.42 and 18.55 agree with the published wording as far as the unit’s extent allows (18.42 matches odyssey-080.363 exactly); 18.59 now agrees with odyssey-075.438. Nothing further.
15. **Passages scanned for flags.** The packet lists none; scanning was not required and no metrical sentence added.

### gloss-parse check

Method: every key of `gloss.json` (157 novel forms and the `__broaden__` block of 18 keys, now 21) was set against every line it occurs in (case, tense, mood, person, number; the voice and the construction named), then checked for: lemma as LSJ gives it, Attic equivalent named for every Homeric form, homographs joined by ‘ · ’, no line numbers, no ‘here’ used to pin a line, typographic ’ only (no ASCII ' or backtick), under 230 characters (all novel entries now fit; the longest is below the limit), nothing line-pinned. Every `__broaden__` value begins with the old entry from `known-forms.json` whole, then ‘ · ’ and the new reading (checked by script for all 21). Known forms in this part were also read against their existing entries (about 330 forms); gaps found are listed under Broadened.

Corrected (all by script, in `gloss.json`):

### new-renderings.md against units.json

All twelve rows now in `new-renderings.md` match the English in `units.json` in both layers, after the changes above: 18.25 (l “And him, enraged, addressed Irus the vagrant:”, i “Then Irus the vagrant, enraged, spoke to him:”), 18.51, 18.73 Ἶρος Ἄϊρος (l “Irus, Un-Irus”, i “Irus, who will be Irus no more”), ἐπίσπαστον κακόν, 18.27 γρηῒ καμινοῖ (“like an old furnace-woman” / “just like …”), 18.26 ἐπιτροχάδην, 18.2 γαστὴρ μάργη (“a frenzied belly” / “a ravenous belly”), 18.45 κνίσης ἐμπλήσαντες (“having filled them with fat” … “fat and blood” / “after stuffing them with fat and blood”), 18.79 βουγάϊε, 18.106 κοίρανος, 18.76 δρηστῆρες, 18.58 ἀπώμνυον (and the note at 58 gives the ἀπο- sense). The two stale rows pass 1 flagged (18.50, and 18.69–70 `l` “standing close beside”) are no longer in the file; the units follow the shipped wording for both, so nothing to fix. No row was changed in this pass. The two house-table conflicts found in this pass (λυγρός, ἐρίζω) are table rows, not new renderings, so they needed a change in `units.json` and not a new row.

### Findings considered and refused (pass 2)

1. **Pass 1's refusal 2 (ἐρίζετον `i` “challenging”)**: reversed above, because the table's row for ἐρίζω fixes “rival”.
2. **Homographs ἕλκε (impf. and imperative) and δύῃ (δύη dative and δύω subjunctive)**: real homographs, but neither second reading occurs in this part and the key is not ambiguous in it; adding them would be speculation. Left.
3. **ἐάσομεν (49, `we will allow`)**: the old entry's ‘let, allow’ and ‘we will let (him) be’ cover the use; a third reading adds nothing. Left.
4. **ἀπώμνυον (58): old entry ‘swear, take an oath’ against the note's ‘swear not to’**: the table (10.345, 12.303) fixes “swore”, and the row for 12.303 avoids “swore to refrain”; the entry gives the dictionary meaning and the note explains the ἀπο-. Left.
5. **αἵδ ‘this (here)’ and ἐνταυθοῖ ‘here, to this very spot’**: ‘here’ is the meaning of the word, not a pin to a line (the known entry for ὅδε has the same wording). Left.
6. **ἀρναῖος ‘later replaced by Ἶρος’, ἀντίνοός, ἶρος ‘the town beggar’**: identifications of a proper name, not parses tied to a line. Left.
7. **ἐπιτροχάδην ‘at a run’ in the entry**: a literal gloss of the word's formation, not an English rendering of the word in the text. Left.
8. **ἐνένιπεν, ἔπος τ’ ἔφατ’ ἔκ τ’ ὀνόμαζεν (78)**: `l`/`i` match the 16.417 row (“rebuked … and spoke a word and called him by name”). Left.
9. **i of 73 begins “Soon …” and drops ἦ ‘truly’**: the first clause of the row's wording must stand as written and ἦ here is a mild affirmation; the `l` has “Truly”. Left.
10. **Pass 1's refusals 1, 3 to 13 and 15 (ὁράασθαι; κακοείμονας; ὑπερφιάλως; ἀνελόντα; ἥ μιν ἱκάνει; ἐπιγνώωσι; ἕλκε; Ἶρις; remarks at 12 and 22; the sausage; ἐπιλλίζουσιν; βαλὼν ἐν νηί; repeated lines)**: re-read against the lines, the table and the notes; they stand.
11. **Other capital letters after ; or : (13 `l`/`i` “You seem”, 54 `l` “If this man”, 46 “And thus”, 41 “I am”)**: the published parts use both after ;, and a pronoun or a new sentence after : takes a capital; each is consistent in its own layer. Left, except the five clear mismatches fixed above.
12. **“bane of all mortals” (δηλήμων, 83)**: matches the house “the bane of ships” (δηλήματα νηῶν, 12.286). Left.
13. **“Strange man”, “lordly suitors”, “noble suitors”, “the sacred strength of Antinous”, “the strong, sacred figure of Telemachus”, “manly spirit” / “proud spirit”, “a mighty oath” / “a solemn oath”, “beyond measure”, “staff”, “genitals”, “the portico”, “the forecourt”, “scrounger” (not “vagrant”)**: each looked up in the table; all follow it.
